title: Mathematical Operations
shortDescription: Symbol substitution, defined operators, interchanges and BODMAS with coded signs.
genZNote: Same maths, new costumes: plus becomes times, minus becomes divide. Translate first, calculate second.

sections.heading: Symbol Substitution
sections.body: Replace the coded symbols with their real operations first, then apply BODMAS (Brackets, Orders, Division/Multiplication, Addition/Subtraction). Example: If + means ×, − means ÷, × means −, ÷ means +, then 8 + 6 − 3 × 2 ÷ 4 becomes 8 × 6 ÷ 3 − 2 + 4 = 16 − 2 + 4 = 18.

sections.heading: Defined Operators
bullets: If a * b = a² − b, then 4 * 3 = 13.
Nested: evaluate brackets first (a ⊕ b) ⊕ c.
Check whether the operator is commutative before swapping terms.

sections.heading: Interchange and Equation Balancing
bullets: Interchange of signs/numbers: make the swap on the given equation and verify the equality.
Find the correct signs for a statement such as 6 ? 3 ? 2 = 4.
Missing operator: try ÷ and × first; use trial combinations.
Use BODMAS carefully: multiplication and division before addition/subtraction from left to right.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Mathematical operations questions re-define symbols or operators and test BODMAS under the new definitions.

highYieldFacts: Do not apply BODMAS before translating.
commonTraps: Do not assume a defined operator is commutative.

sources.name: Standard competitive-exam reasoning reference (R.S. Aggarwal, Verbal & Non-Verbal Reasoning)
